Oxidation state: $+5$; prepared by heating Orthophosphoric Acid ($\\text{H}_3\\text{PO}_4$) to $\\sim 250^\\circ\\text{C}$ to eliminate a water molecule between two acid molecules.
Oxidation state: $+1$; prepared by dissolving phosphorus in nitric acid.
Oxidation state: $0$; prepared by subliming white phosphorus.
e: Explanation: Option 0 misidentifies the oxidation state as $+3$ (which belongs to phosphorous acid). Option 1 is correct because in **Pyrophosphoric Acid ($\\text{H}_4\\text{P}_2\\text{O}_7$)**, phosphorus exhibits an oxidation state of **$+5$** [$4(+1) + 2(x) + 7(-2) = 0 \\rightarrow 2x = 10 \\rightarrow x = +5$]. It is synthesized by the **Thermal Condensation** of two molecules of orthophosphoric acid ($\\text{H}_3\\text{PO}_4$) heated to $\\sim 250^\\circ\\text{C}$, driving off one molecule of water: $2\\text{H}_3\\text{PO}_4 \\xrightarrow{\\Delta} \\text{H}_4\\text{P}_2\\text{O}_7 + \\text{H}_2\\text{O}$. It contains four ionizable $-\\text{OH}$ groups (tetrabasic). Option 2 and Option 3 list incorrect $+1$ or zero oxidation states.

qe: Molecular oxygen ($\\text{O}_2$) exhibits physical magnetism despite possessing an even number of total electrons (16 electrons). What magnetic property defines $\\text{O}_2$, and why does it exhibit this behavior?
qh: कुल इलेक्ट्रॉनों (16 इलेक्ट्रॉन) की सम संख्या होने के बावजूद आणविक ऑक्सीजन ($\\text{O}_2$) भौतिक चुंबकत्व प्रदर्शित करता है। कौन सा चुंबकीय गुण $\\text{O}_2$ को परिभाषित करता है, और यह इस व्यवहार को क्यों प्रदर्शित करता है?
o: Diamagnetic; because all 16 electrons are paired in molecular bonding orbitals.
Paramagnetic; because its molecular orbital configuration contains two unpaired electrons in degenerate antibonding $\\pi^*$ orbitals ($\\pi^*_{2p_x}$ and $\\pi^*_{2p_y}$).
Ferromagnetic; because it forms permanent domain magnets at room temperature.
Antiferromagnetic; because it repels external magnetic fields completely.
e: Explanation: Option 0 incorrectly predicts diamagnetism based on simple Lewis dot structures, a classic failure of valence bond theory. Option 1 is correct because according to **Molecular Orbital Theory (MOT)**, the 16 valence electrons of the $\\text{O}_2$ molecule fill orbitals up to the antibonding level, placing the last two electrons into degenerate **Antibonding $\\pi^*$ Orbitals ($\\pi^*_{2p_x}^1 = \\pi^*_{2p_y}^1$)** with parallel spins according to Hund's rule. The presence of these two **Unpaired Electrons** renders molecular oxygen **Paramagnetic** [attracted into an external magnetic field]. Liquid oxygen is noticeably attracted to the poles of a strong magnet. Option 2 and Option 3 list bulk solid magnetic states.

qe: The stratospheric ozone layer absorbs harmful solar ultraviolet (UV) radiation. What specific class of synthetic industrial compounds is primarily responsible for the catalytic depletion of stratospheric ozone?
qh: समतापमंडलीय ओजोन परत हानिकारक सौर पराबैंगनी (UV) विकिरण को अवशोषित करती है। सिंथेटिक औद्योगिक यौगिकों की कौन सी विशिष्ट श्रेणी समतापमंडलीय ओजोन के उत्प्रेरक क्षरण (catalytic depletion) के लिए मुख्य रूप से जिम्मेदार है?
o: Heavy metal amalgams like lead-mercury complexes.
Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs, such as Freon-12) releasing reactive chlorine free radicals ($\\text{Cl}^\\bullet$) under photolytic solar UV degradation.
Potassium nitrate fertilizer runoff in rivers.
Silicone polymers used in cosmetics.
e: Explanation: Option 0 describes heavy metal toxins that do not reach the stratosphere. Option 1 is correct because **Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)** (such as $\\text{CF}_2\\text{Cl}_2$, Freon-12) used as refrigerants and aerosol propellants diffuse into the stratosphere. There, intense solar UV radiation causes **Photolytic Homolysis**, releasing reactive **Chlorine Free Radicals ($\\text{Cl}^\\bullet$)**: $\\text{CF}_2\\text{Cl}_2 \\xrightarrow{h\\nu} \\text{CF}_2\\text{Cl}^\\bullet + \\text{Cl}^\\bullet$. These chlorine radicals initiate a catalytic chain reaction that breaks down ozone molecules into oxygen: $\\text{Cl}^\\bullet + \\text{O}_3 \\rightarrow \\text{ClO}^\\bullet + \\text{O}_2$, depleting the protective stratospheric ozone layer. Option 2 and Option 3 list aquatic eutrophication agents or inert polymers.

qe: Evaluating the thermodynamic stability and phase transitions of elemental sulfur allotropes reveals a specific temperature threshold. What is the transition temperature at which yellow rhombic ($\alpha$-sulfur) and monoclinic ($\beta$-sulfur) exist in equilibrium, and what molecular species dominates in sulfur vapor at elevated temperatures?
qh: सल्फर अपररूपों की ऊष्मागतिक स्थिरता और चरण परिवर्तनों का मूल्यांकन एक विशिष्ट तापमान सीमा को दर्शाता है। वह संक्रमण तापमान क्या है जिस पर पीला विषमलंबाक्ष ($\alpha$-सल्फर) और एकनताक्ष ($\beta$-सल्फर) साम्यावस्था में सह-अस्तित्व में रहते हैं, और उच्च तापमान पर सल्फर वाष्प में कौन सी आणविक प्रजाति हावी होती है?
o: Transition Temperature: $273\text{ K}$; Dominant Vapor Species: Ring $\text{S}_8$ (diamagnetic)
Transition Temperature: $369\text{ K}$; Dominant Vapor Species: Diatomic $\text{S}_2$ (paramagnetic like $\text{O}_2$)
Transition Temperature: $450\text{ K}$; Dominant Vapor Species: Triatomic $\text{S}_3$ (ferromagnetic)
Transition Temperature: $523\text{ K}$; Dominant Vapor Species: Ionic $\text{S}^{2-}$ (antiferromagnetic)
e: Explanation: Option 0 incorrectly identifies the transition threshold as $273\text{ K}$ and misidentifies $\text{S}_8$ as the high-temperature vapor species. Option 1 is correct because **Rhombic Sulfur ($\alpha$-sulfur)** (stable below $369\text{ K}$) and **Monoclinic Sulfur ($\beta$-sulfur)** (stable above $369\text{ K}$) exist in thermodynamic equilibrium at **$369\text{ K}$**, which is defined as their **Transition Temperature** [the precise temperature at which two crystalline allotropic forms of an element coexist in equilibrium at standard pressure]. Furthermore, at high temperatures ($\\sim 1000\text{ K}$), sulfur vapor consists predominantly of **Diatomic $\text{S}_2$ Molecules**, which contain two unpaired electrons in antibonding $\pi^*$ molecular orbitals, rendering $\text{S}_2$ **Paramagnetic** [attracted into an external magnetic field], behaving exactly like molecular oxygen ($\text{O}_2$). Option 2 and Option 3 propose non-existent transition thresholds or magnetic states.

qe: Sulphur dioxide ($\text{SO}_2$) and chlorine gas ($\text{Cl}_2$) are both deployed as industrial bleaching agents for paper, cotton, and textiles. What fundamental chemical mechanism distinguishes the bleaching action of $\text{SO}_2$ from that of $\text{Cl}_2$?
qh: सल्फर डाइऑक्साइड ($\text{SO}_2$) और क्लोरीन गैस ($\text{Cl}_2$) दोनों को कागज, कपास और वस्त्रों के लिए औद्योगिक विरंजन (bleaching) एजेंटों के रूप में तैनात किया जाता है। कौन सा मौलिक रासायनिक तंत्र $\text{SO}_2$ की विरंजन क्रिया को $\text{Cl}_2$ से अलग करता है?
o: $\text{SO}_2$ bleaches permanently via oxidation; $\text{Cl}_2$ bleaches temporarily via reduction.
$\text{SO}_2$ bleaches temporarily via reduction (removing oxygen from colored matter); $\text{Cl}_2$ bleaches permanently in the presence of moisture via oxidation (generating nascent oxygen).
$\text{SO}_2$ bleaches by subliming colored pigments into dry ice; $\text{Cl}_2$ bleaches by precipitating sulfur.
Both $\text{SO}_2$ and $\text{Cl}_2$ bleach permanently via identical catalytic dehydration pathways.
e: Explanation: Option 0 reverses the redox mechanics and permanence of $\text{SO}_2$ and $\text{Cl}_2$. Option 1 is correct because **Sulphur Dioxide ($\text{SO}_2$)** acts as a **Reducing Bleaching Agent** [a chemical that removes oxygen or adds hydrogen to organic chromophores], converting colored matter into colorless reduced forms; exposure to atmospheric oxygen re-oxidizes the chromophores, making the bleaching action **temporary**. Conversely, **Chlorine ($\text{Cl}_2$)** acts as an **Oxidizing Bleaching Agent** in the presence of moisture, reacting with water to release **Nascent Oxygen** [$\text{Cl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{HCl} + [\text{O}]$], which permanently destroys organic color pigments via irreversible oxidation. Option 2 and Option 3 describe non-existent sublimation or identical mechanisms.

qe: In the industrial manufacture of Sulphuric Acid ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$), two distinct classical pathways are utilized. What catalytic systems differentiate the Contact Process from the Lead Chamber Process?
qh: सल्फ्यूरिक अम्ल ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$) के औद्योगिक निर्माण में, दो विशिष्ट शास्त्रीय मार्गों का उपयोग किया जाता है। संपर्क प्रक्रिया (Contact Process) को सीस कक्ष प्रक्रिया (Lead Chamber Process) से कौन सी उत्प्रेरक प्रणालियाँ अलग करती हैं?
o: Contact Process: Catalyzed by oxides of nitrogen; Lead Chamber Process: Catalyzed by platinum or $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$.
Contact Process: Catalyzed by Vanadium Pentoxide ($\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$) or Platinum ($\text{Pt}$); Lead Chamber Process: Catalyzed by Oxides of Nitrogen (homogeneous catalysis).
Contact Process: Catalyzed by zeolites; Lead Chamber Process: Catalyzed by activated charcoal.
Both processes use liquid mercury as an essential homogeneous catalyst.
e: Explanation: Option 0 reverses the catalyst assignments between the two industrial processes. Option 1 is correct because both processes oxidize $\text{SO}_2$ to $\text{SO}_3$ but rely on different **Catalytic Systems**: the **Contact Process** uses heterogeneous solid catalysts, primarily **Vanadium Pentoxide ($\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$)** (or platinized asbestos), to achieve high yield at $720\text{ K}$; the historical **Lead Chamber Process** utilizes gas-phase **Oxides of Nitrogen** (NO / $\text{NO}_2$) to drive **Homogeneous Catalysis** [a catalytic reaction where the catalyst and reactants exist in the same physical phase]. Option 2 and Option 3 list incorrect zeolite, charcoal, or liquid mercury catalysts.

qe: Oleum, also known as fuming sulphuric acid, is an essential industrial intermediate in chemical synthesis. What is the chemical formula of Oleum (Pyrosulphuric Acid), and how is it produced?
qh: ओलियम (Oleum), जिसे सधूम सल्फ्यूरिक अम्ल (fuming sulphuric acid) भी कहा जाता है, रासायनिक संश्लेषण में एक आवश्यक औद्योगिक मध्यवर्ती है। ओलियम (पायरोसल्फ्यूरिक अम्ल) का रासायनिक सूत्र क्या है, और इसका उत्पादन कैसे किया जाता है?
o: Formula: $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$; produced by electrolyzing cold concentrated sulphuric acid.
Formula: $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_7$; produced by dissolving Sulphur Trioxide ($\text{SO}_3$) gas into concentrated Sulphuric Acid ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$).
Formula: $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_3$; produced by passing hydrogen sulfide gas through water.
Formula: $\text{H}_2\text{S}_4\text{O}_6$; produced by reacting sulfur powder with nitric acid.
e: Explanation: Option 0 gives the formula for Peroxodisulphuric acid (Marshall's acid, $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$). Option 1 is correct because **Oleum (Pyrosulphuric Acid)** has the chemical formula **$\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_7$**. It is produced during the final absorption stage of the Contact Process by absorbing gaseous **Sulphur Trioxide ($\text{SO}_3$)** directly into 98% concentrated **Sulphuric Acid ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$)**: $\text{SO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_7$. Direct dissolution of $\text{SO}_3$ in water is avoided because it forms a dense, unmanageable acid mist. Diluting oleum with controlled amounts of water yields pure $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$. Option 2 lists sulphurous acid, and Option 3 lists tetrathionic acid.

qe: Peroxodisulphuric Acid ($\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$), commonly known as Marshall's acid, contains a specific structural oxygen link. What chemical transformation produces Marshall's acid at the anode during the electrolysis of sulphuric acid?
qh: पेरॉक्सोडाइसल्फ्यूरिक अम्ल ($\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$), जिसे आमतौर पर मार्शल के अम्ल (Marshall's acid) के रूप में जाना जाता है, में एक विशिष्ट संरचनात्मक ऑक्सीजन लिंक होता है। सल्फ्यूरिक अम्ल के इलेक्ट्रोलाइटिस के दौरान एनोड पर कौन सा रासायनिक परिवर्तन मार्शल का अम्ल उत्पन्न करता है?
o: Hydrolysis of sulfur dioxide at low voltage.
Anodic oxidation and coupling of bisulphate ions ($\text{HSO}_4^-$) during the electrolysis of pure, cold concentrated sulphuric acid.
Direct reaction of hydrogen sulfide gas with ozone.
Thermal decomposition of oleum in an electric furnace.
e: Explanation: Option 0 misidentifies sulfur dioxide hydrolysis as the electrolytic route. Option 1 is correct because **Marshall's Acid (Peroxodisulphuric Acid, $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$)** contains a characteristic **Peroxide Linkage** ($-\text{O}-\text{O}-$). It is synthesized via **Anodic Oxidation** [an electrolytic process where an anion loses electrons at the positive electrode, undergoing oxidative coupling] by electrolyzing cold, concentrated ($\\sim 50\%$) sulphuric acid or hydrogen sulphate solution at high current density: $2\text{HSO}_4^- \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8 + 2e^-$. Option 2 and Option 3 list incorrect gas-phase oxidation or thermal decomposition paths.

qe: Evaluating Group-17 halogen reactivity reveals unique chemical exceptions. Which halogen is the most electronegative element in the Modern Periodic Table, and what specific nuclear utility does its compound Oxygen Difluoride (or $\text{O}_2\text{F}_2$) perform in processing spent nuclear fuel?
qh: समूह-17 के हैलोजन प्रतिक्रियाशीलता का मूल्यांकन अद्वितीय रासायनिक अपवादों को प्रकट करता है। आधुनिक आवर्त सारणी में कौन सा हैलोजन सबसे अधिक विद्युतऋणात्मक तत्व है, और इसका यौगिक ऑक्सीजन डाइफ्लोराइड (या $\text{O}_2\text{F}_2$) प्रयुक्त परमाणु ईंधन (spent nuclear fuel) के प्रसंस्करण में क्या विशिष्ट परमाणु उपयोग करता है?
o: Chlorine; oxidizes uranium to $\text{UCl}_6$
Fluorine; $\text{O}_2\text{F}_2$ acts as a strong fluorinating agent that oxidizes Plutonium to volatile Plutonium Hexafluoride ($\text{PuF}_6$), removing plutonium from spent fuel.
Bromine; converts radioactive cesium into stable lead
Iodine; precipitates thorium as insoluble iodide
e: Explanation: Option 0 incorrectly identifies chlorine as the most electronegative element (Fluorine has the highest Pauling electronegativity, 4.0). Option 1 is correct because **Fluorine ($ ext{F}$)** is the most electronegative and reactive non-metal. Its oxide derivative, **Dioxygen Difluoride ($ ext{O}_2 ext{F}_2$)**, serves as a powerful **Fluorinating Agent** [a specialized reagent capable of transferring fluorine atoms to other chemical species]. In nuclear chemistry, $ ext{O}_2 ext{F}_2$ reacts with solid plutonium residues in spent nuclear fuel rods to form volatile **Plutonium Hexafluoride ($ ext{PuF}_6$)**, allowing plutonium to be separated and recovered via fluorination. Option 2 and Option 3 propose impossible nuclear transmutations.

qe: Chlorine gas ($\text{Cl}_2$) is manufactured on a massive industrial scale using specific electrochemical and catalytic processes. What choices correctly identify Deacon's Process and the electrolysis of brine in a Nelson Cell?
qh: क्लोरीन गैस ($\text{Cl}_2$) का निर्माण विशिष्ट इलेक्ट्रोकेमिकल और उत्प्रेरक प्रक्रियाओं का उपयोग करके बड़े पैमाने पर औद्योगिक पैमाने पर किया जाता है। Deacon की प्रक्रिया और Nelson Cell में ब्राइन के इलेक्ट्रोलाइटिस की सही पहचान कौन से विकल्प करते हैं?
o: Deacon's Process: Oxidation of $\text{HCl}$ gas by atmospheric oxygen over a $\text{CuCl}_2$ catalyst; Nelson Cell: Electrolysis of aqueous $\text{NaCl}$ (brine).
Deacon's Process: Electrolysis of molten calcium fluoride; Nelson Cell: Reduction of bleaching powder with ammonia.
Deacon's Process: Heating potassium chlorate with charcoal; Nelson Cell: Distillation of liquid air.
Both processes rely on the thermal decomposition of sodium nitrate.
e: Explanation: Option 1 misidentifies Deacon's process as fluoride electrolysis. Option 0 is correct because **Chlorine ($\text{Cl}_2$)** is industrially manufactured via two classic methods: (1) **Deacon's Process**, which involves the catalytic gas-phase oxidation of hydrogen chloride gas ($\text{HCl}$) by atmospheric oxygen at $723\text{ K}$ using a **Cupric Chloride ($\text{CuCl}_2$) Catalyst**: $4\text{HCl} + \text{O}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{CuCl}_2} 2\text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$; and (2) **Nelson Cell / Castner-Kellner Process**, which electrolyzes concentrated aqueous sodium chloride solution (**Brine**): $2\text{NaCl} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{electrolysis}} \text{Cl}_2\uparrow + \text{H}_2\uparrow + 2\text{NaOH}$. Option 2 and Option 3 describe chlorate heating or fractional air distillation.

qe: Bromine ($\text{Br}$, $Z=35$) is the only non-metallic element that exists as a liquid at room temperature. What is its principal natural source in India, and what specific potassium salt of bromine is prescribed medically as a central nervous system sedative and pain reliever?
qh: ब्रोमीन ($\text{Br}$, $Z=35$) एकमात्र गैर-धातु तत्व है जो कमरे के तापमान पर तरल रूप में मौजूद होता है। भारत में इसका मुख्य प्राकृतिक स्रोत क्या है, और ब्रोमीन के किस विशिष्ट पोटेशियम लवण को केंद्रीय तंत्रिका तंत्र शामक (sedative) और दर्द निवारक के रूप में चिकित्सीय रूप से निर्धारित किया जाता है?
o: Natural Source: Himalayan rock salt; Prescribed Salt: Potassium Fluoride (KF)
Natural Source: Natural brine deposits at the Rann of Kutch; Prescribed Salt: Potassium Bromide (KBr).
Natural Source: Volcanic ash in Sicily; Prescribed Salt: Potassium Iodide (KI)
Natural Source: Bauxite mines in Bihar; Prescribed Salt: Potassium Carbonate
e: Explanation: Option 0 misidentifies Himalayan rock salt as a bromine source. Option 1 is correct because **Bromine ($\text{Br}_2$)** is a dense, reddish-brown liquid. In India, elemental bromine is extracted commercially from the concentrated **Sub-surface Brine Reserves** located in the **Rann of Kutch (Gujarat)** and from carnallite marine residues. Chemically synthesized **Potassium Bromide (KBr)** depresses central nervous system excitability and was historically prescribed as a medical **Sedative** [a drug that induces calm or sleep by depressing central nervous system activity] and pain reliever. Option 2 and Option 3 list volcanic ash or bauxite sources.

qe: Iodine ($\text{I}$, $Z=53$) is a dark violet, lustrous solid that sublimes upon gentle heating. How does iodine function in human physiology, and what pharmaceutical formulation constitutes 'Tincture of Iodine'?
qh: आयोडीन ($\text{I}$, $Z=53$) एक गहरा बैंगनी, चमकदार ठोस है जो हल्के गर्म होने पर ऊर्ध्वपातित (sublimes) हो जाता है। मानव शरीर क्रिया विज्ञान में आयोडीन कैसे कार्य करता है, और कौन सा फार्मास्युटिकल फॉर्मूलेशन 'टिंचर आयोडीन' (Tincture of Iodine) बनाता है?
o: Physiological role: Hemoglobin synthesis; Tincture Iodine: Pure iodine dissolved in concentrated nitric acid.
Physiological role: Component of the thyroid hormone thyroxine; Tincture Iodine: 2-3% solution of Iodine in an Alcohol-Water mixture.
Physiological role: Structural constituent of bone hydroxyapatite; Tincture Iodine: Iodine powder suspended in liquid paraffin.
Physiological role: Drives gastric pepsin digestion; Tincture Iodine: Saturated solution of iodine in acetone.
e: Explanation: Option 0 incorrectly assigns iron's role (hemoglobin) to iodine and mixes it with nitric acid. Option 1 is correct because iodine is an essential trace element required for synthesizing **Thyroxine** ($T_4$) and triiodothyronine ($T_3$), hormones secreted by the **Thyroid Gland** that regulate basal metabolic rate. Iodine deficiency leads to thyroid enlargement (**Goitre**). In pharmacology, **Tincture of Iodine** is an effective topical **Antiseptic** [a chemical agent applied to living tissue to inhibit or kill micro-organisms] composed of a **2-3% solution of Elemental Iodine ($ ext{I}_2$) and Potassium Iodide ($ ext{KI}$) dissolved in an Alcohol-Water solvent mixture**. Option 2 and Option 3 describe bone or gastric digestive functions.

qe: Over-the-counter pain relief ointments like 'Iodex' are commercially marketed for relieving bone and joint injuries. Despite its brown color and name, what is the active chemical component of Iodex, and does it contain elemental iodine?
qh: 'Iodex' जैसे ओवर-द-काउंटर दर्द निवारक मलहम व्यावसायिक रूप से हड्डी और जोड़ों की चोटों से राहत के लिए बेचे जाते हैं। इसके भूरे रंग और नाम के बावजूद, Iodex का सक्रिय रासायनिक घटक क्या है, और क्या इसमें तात्विक आयोडीन होता है?
o: Contains $10\%$ elemental iodine dissolved in liquid mercury amalgam.
Active component: Methyl salicylate / Chlorophenol derivatives (e.g., Dichlorophenol); Contains ZERO elemental iodine.
Active component: Pure potassium iodide crystals dissolved in sulfuric acid.
Active component: Sodium hypochlorite powder mixed with animal charcoal.
e: Explanation: Option 0 succumbs to the brand misnomer and claims Iodex contains elemental iodine and mercury. Option 1 is correct because the commercial pain-relief ointment **Iodex** is a classic pharmaceutical misnomer. Modern formulations of Iodex contain **Methyl Salicylate** and **Dichlorophenol / Chlorophenol Derivatives** as active analgesic and counter-irritant agents. It contains **no elemental iodine ($ ext{I}_2$)**. Its dark color and name were originally derived from early 20th-century formulations, but contemporary preparations rely on non-iodine organic analgesics to treat musculoskeletal inflammation. Option 2 and Option 3 list iodine in sulfuric acid or bleaching agents.

qe: Chlorine forms a series of oxoacids containing chlorine in different oxidation states ($+1, +3, +5, +7$). Which chlorine oxoacid is the thermodynamically strongest oxoacid, and what structural factor accounts for its extreme acidity?
qh: क्लोरीन विभिन्न ऑक्सीकरण अवस्थाओं ($+1, +3, +5, +7$) में क्लोरीन युक्त ऑक्सोअम्लों की एक श्रृंखला बनाता है। कौन सा क्लोरीन ऑक्सोअम्ल ऊष्मागतिकी रूप से सबसे मजबूत ऑक्सोअम्ल है, और कौन सा संरचनात्मक कारक इसकी अत्यधिक अम्लता का कारण है?
o: Hypochlorous acid ($\text{HClO}$); stabilized by weak hydrogen bonding.

Perchloric Acid ($\text{HClO}_4$); chlorine is in its maximum $+7$ oxidation state, and its conjugate base ($\text{ClO}_4^-$) is stabilized by extensive resonance delocalization of negative charge across four equivalent oxygen atoms.
Chlorous acid ($\text{HClO}_2$); stabilized by $sp^3d$ hybridization.
Chloric acid ($\text{HClO}_3$); stabilized by forming a dimer in liquid state.
e: Explanation: Option 0 misidentifies hypochlorous acid ($\text{HClO}$), which is actually the weakest oxoacid in the series. Option 1 is correct because **Perchloric Acid ($\text{HClO}_4$)** is the **Strongest Oxoacid of Chlorine** (and one of the strongest inorganic Brønsted acids). In $\text{HClO}_4$, chlorine sits in its maximum oxidation state of **$+7$**. Upon losing a proton, the resulting **Perchlorate Anion ($\text{ClO}_4^-$)** is exceptionally stable because its negative charge is spread equally over four electronegative oxygen atoms via **Resonance Delocalization** [the dispersal of electron density over multiple bonded atoms in a conjugated polyatomic ion, lowering its potential energy]. Acidity increases strictly with increasing oxygen atoms: $\text{HClO} < \text{HClO}_2 < \text{HClO}_3 < \text{HClO}_4$. Option 2 and Option 3 list weaker oxoacids.

qe: Gaseous chlorine dioxide ($\text{ClO}_2$) is an important industrial bleach and water disinfectant. What term defines a chemical mixture of $\text{ClO}_2$ and $\text{Cl}_2$ gas, and what is its primary industrial application?
qh: गैसीय क्लोरीन डाइऑक्साइड ($\text{ClO}_2$) एक महत्वपूर्ण औद्योगिक ब्लीच और पानी कीटाणुनाशक है। कौन सा शब्द $\text{ClO}_2$ और $\text{Cl}_2$ गैस के रासायनिक मिश्रण को परिभाषित करता है, और इसका प्राथमिक औद्योगिक अनुप्रयोग क्या है?
o: Term: Aqua Regia; used to dissolve pure gold bullion.
Term: Euchlorine; used as a powerful bleaching agent for paper pulp, textiles, and municipal water purification.
Term: Producer Gas; used as a blast furnace fuel.
Term: Fuming Oleum; used to synthesize rubber.
e: Explanation: Option 0 describes aqua regia ($\text{HCl} + \text{HNO}_3$). Option 1 is correct because a gaseous mixture composed of **Chlorine Dioxide ($\text{ClO}_2$) and Chlorine Gas ($\text{Cl}_2$)** is commercially and historically termed **Euchlorine**. It is synthesized by reacting potassium chlorate ($\text{KClO}_3$) with concentrated hydrochloric acid. Euchlorine acts as a potent oxidizing mixture used for **Bleaching Wood Pulp** in paper manufacturing, whitening textiles, and operating as a broad-spectrum disinfectant in municipal water treatment plants. Option 2 describes producer gas ($\text{CO} + \text{N}_2$), and Option 3 describes oleum.

qe: Analytical determination of carbon monoxide (CO) gas concentrations in environmental and industrial gas streams relies on a specific halogen oxide reagent. Which halogen oxide quantitatively oxidizes CO to $\text{CO}_2$?
qh: पर्यावरण और औद्योगिक गैस धाराओं में कार्बन मोनोऑक्साइड (CO) गैस सांद्रता का विश्लेषणात्मक निर्धारण एक विशिष्ट हैलोजन ऑक्साइड अभिकर्मक पर निर्भर करता है। कौन सा हैलोजन ऑक्साइड CO को $\text{CO}_2$ में मात्रात्मक रूप से (quantitatively) ऑक्सीकृत करता है?
o: Dichlorine monoxide ($\text{Cl}_2\text{O}$)
Iodine Pentoxide ($\text{I}_2\text{O}_5$)
Fluorine monoxide ($\text{F}_2\text{O}$)
Bromine dioxide ($\text{BrO}_2$)
e: Explanation: Option 0 misidentifies chlorine monoxide as the quantitative CO reagent. Option 1 is correct because **Iodine Pentoxide ($\text{I}_2\text{O}_5$)** is a white crystalline solid that acts as a reliable oxidizing agent. It reacts quantitatively with carbon monoxide gas at $170^\circ\text{C}$, converting CO into carbon dioxide gas while being reduced itself to elemental iodine: $\text{I}_2\text{O}_5 + 5\text{CO} \rightarrow \text{I}_2 + 5\text{CO}_2$. By titrating the liberated iodine ($\text{I}_2$) with standard sodium thiosulphate solution (hypo), analytical chemists calculate the precise concentration of toxic CO present in air samples. Option 2 and Option 3 list oxides that do not react quantitatively with CO.

qe: Noble gases (Group-18) were long considered completely chemically inert. Which noble gas was the first to be synthesized into a true chemical compound by Neil Bartlett in 1962, and what was the chemical formula of that compound?
qh: उत्कृष्ट गैसों (समूह-18) को लंबे समय से पूरी तरह से रासायनिक रूप से अक्रिय माना जाता था। 1962 में नील बार्टलेट द्वारा किस उत्कृष्ट गैस का पहले सच्चे रासायनिक यौगिक के रूप में संश्लेषण किया गया था, और उस यौगिक का रासायनिक सूत्र क्या था?
o: Helium; formula: $\text{HePtF}_6$
Xenon; formula: $\text{Xe}^+[\text{PtF}_6]^-$ (Xenon Hexafluoroplatinate)
Radon; formula: $\text{RnCl}_2$
Argon; formula: $\text{ArO}_3$
e: Explanation: Option 0 incorrectly selects helium (helium has the highest ionization enthalpy and forms no neutral molecular ground-state compounds). Option 1 is correct because in 1962, English chemist **Neil Bartlett** noticed that platinum hexafluoride ($\text{PtF}_6$) oxidized molecular oxygen to form $\text{O}_2^+[\text{PtF}_6]^-$. Realizing that the first ionization enthalpy of **Xenon** ($1170\text{ kJ/mol}$) is almost identical to that of oxygen ($1175\text{ kJ/mol}$), Bartlett reacted xenon gas with $\text{PtF}_6$ vapor to synthesize the world's first true noble gas compound: **Xenon Hexafluoroplatinate ($\text{Xe}^+[\text{PtF}_6]^-$, a red-orange crystalline solid)**. Option 2 and Option 3 list non-existent early discovery compounds.

qe: Radon ($Z=86$, $A=222$) is a radioactive noble gas located in Group-18. Unlike other noble gases (He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe) that are harvested directly from atmospheric air, how is Radon produced naturally in the environment?
qh: रेडॉन ($Z=86$, $A=222$) समूह-18 में स्थित एक रेडियोधर्मी उत्कृष्ट गैस है। अन्य उत्कृष्ट गैसों (He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe) के विपरीत जिन्हें सीधे वायुमंडलीय हवा से काटा जाता है, पर्यावरण में प्राकृतिक रूप से रेडॉन का उत्पादन कैसे होता है?
o: Harvested from fractional distillation of liquid water.
Formed as a natural radioactive alpha-decay daughter product of Radium-226 ($^{226}\text{Ra}$).
Produced by cosmic ray bombardment of nitrogen in the upper atmosphere.
Synthesized by burning sulfur in electric arc furnaces.
e: Explanation: Option 0 claims radon is obtained from water distillation. Option 1 is correct because all noble gases except Radon occur in trace amounts in atmospheric air and are harvested as byproducts during the liquefaction and fractional distillation of air. **Radon ($^{222}\text{Rn}$)** is a short-lived radioactive gas (half-life $3.82\text{ days}$) that exists in minute quantities in soil and rock because it is generated continuously as a **Radioactive Decay Product** via the alpha-decay of Radium-226 ($^{226}\text{Ra} \rightarrow {}^{222}\text{Rn} + {}^4\text{He}$). Option 2 describes radiocarbon production, and Option 3 describes sulfur oxidation.

qe: Noble gas atoms can be trapped inside host crystal structures without forming true chemical covalent or ionic bonds. What term defines these physical inclusion complexes, and which noble gases fail to form them due to small atomic size?
qh: उत्कृष्ट गैस परमाणुओं को सच्चे रासायनिक सहसंयोजक या आयनिक बंध बनाए बिना होस्ट क्रिस्टल संरचनाओं के भीतर फंसाया जा सकता है। कौन सा शब्द इन भौतिक समावेशन परिसरों को परिभाषित करता है, और कौन सी उत्कृष्ट गैसें छोटे परमाणु आकार के कारण इन्हें बनाने में विफल रहती हैं?
o: Term: Coordination polymers; Failed gases: Xenon and Radon
Term: Clathrate Compounds (Cage Compounds); Failed gases: Helium and Neon
Term: Amalgams; Failed gases: Argon and Krypton
Term: Organometallics; Failed gases: Radon and Helium
e: Explanation: Option 0 misidentifies the inclusion complexes as coordination polymers. Option 1 is correct because **Clathrate Compounds (Cage Compounds)** are supramolecular inclusion complexes where guest noble gas atoms are physically trapped inside cage-like cavities formed by the hydrogen-bonded crystal lattices of organic host molecules (such as quinol or ice). No formal chemical bonds exist between the host and guest. Larger noble gases (Ar, Kr, Xe) fit securely into these cavities. However, **Helium (He) and Neon (Ne)** have exceptionally **Small Atomic Radii**, allowing them to slip out of the host crystal cavities without being trapped, making He and Ne incapable of forming clathrates. Option 2 lists amalgams (mercury alloys), and Option 3 lists organometallics.

qe: Black powder, or gunpowder, is a historic chemical explosive used in pyrotechnics and military applications. What choice correctly identifies the three essential ingredients that constitute gunpowder?
qh: काला पाउडर (ब्लैक पाउडर), या बारूद (gunpowder), पाइरोटेक्निक्स और सैन्य अनुप्रयोगों में इस्तेमाल किया जाने वाला एक ऐतिहासिक रासायनिक विस्फोटक है। कौन सा विकल्प उन तीन आवश्यक सामग्रियों की सही पहचान करता है जो बारूद बनाती हैं?
o: Sulfur, Nitroglycerine, and Lead Acetate
Sulfur, Charcoal (carbon), and Potassium Nitrate (Indian Saltpetre, $\text{KNO}_3$)
Sodium azide, White phosphorus, and Calcium carbide
Chlorine gas, Ammonia, and Mercury fulminate
e: Explanation: Option 0 includes nitroglycerine, which is a modern liquid explosive used in dynamite, not traditional black powder. Option 1 is correct because classic **Gunpowder (Black Powder)** is a solid pyrotechnic mixture composed of three key ingredients: **Potassium Nitrate ($\text{KNO}_3$, $75\%$)**, which acts as the oxidizing agent; **Charcoal (Carbon, $15\%$)**, which acts as the primary fuel; and **Sulfur ($10\%$)**, which lowers the ignition temperature and accelerates reaction kinetics. Upon ignition, the rapid oxidation of carbon and sulfur generates nitrogen and carbon dioxide gases under immense pressure. Option 2 and Option 3 list airbags, matchstick, or toxic war gas precursors.

qe: Hydrogen sulfide gas ($\text{H}_2\text{S}$) is released during volcanic eruptions and organic decomposition. What is its characteristic physical odor, and what chemical reagent acts as the functional anhydride of an aqueous hydrogen sulfide solution?
qh: हाइड्रोजन सल्फाइड गैस ($\text{H}_2\text{S}$) ज्वालामुखी विस्फोट और कार्बनिक अपघटन के दौरान मुक्त होती है। इसकी विशिष्ट भौतिक गंध क्या है, और कौन सा रासायनिक अभिकर्मक जलीय हाइड्रोजन सल्फाइड घोल के कार्यात्मक एनहाइड्राइड के रूप में कार्य करता है?
o: Odor: Fruity smell; Anhydride: Concentrated nitric acid
Odor: Pungent rotten egg smell; Anhydride: Aqueous chlorine solution
Odor: Sweet aromatic smell; Anhydride: Liquid ammonia
Odor: Odorless; Anhydride: Sodium hydroxide
e: Explanation: Option 0 misidentifies the odor as fruity. Option 1 is correct because **Hydrogen Sulfide ($\text{H}_2\text{S}$)** is a colorless, highly toxic gas possessing a powerful, characteristic **Rotten Egg Smell**. It is a weak diprotic acid in water. An **Aqueous Chlorine Solution** acts as its functional chemical precursor/anhydride because chlorine oxidizes hydrogen sulfide or reacts in aqueous systems to displace elemental sulfur: $\text{H}_2\text{S} + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{HCl} + \text{S}\downarrow$. Exposure to high concentrations of $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ paralyzes the olfactory nerve, making it extremely dangerous in industrial settings. Option 2 and Option 3 list sweet or odorless descriptors.

qe: Limestone ($\text{CaCO}_3$) reacts with carbon dioxide to turn lime water clear, but sulphur dioxide ($\text{SO}_2$) exhibits an identical visual precipitation phenomenon with lime water. What chemical compounds cause lime water to turn milky and then clear upon passing excess $\text{SO}_2$ gas?
qh: चूना पत्थर ($\text{CaCO}_3$) चूने के पानी को स्पष्ट करने के लिए कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड के साथ प्रतिक्रिया करता है, लेकिन सल्फर डाइऑक्साइड ($\text{SO}_2$) चूने के पानी के साथ एक समान दृश्य अवक्षेपण घटना प्रदर्शित करता है। अतिरिक्त $\text{SO}_2$ गैस प्रवाहित करने पर कौन से रासायनिक यौगिक चूने के पानी को दूधिया और फिर स्पष्ट बनाते हैं?
o: Milky precipitate: Calcium sulphate; Soluble clear compound: Calcium nitrate
Milky precipitate: Insoluble Calcium Sulphite ($\text{CaSO}_3$); Soluble clear compound: Calcium Bisulphite [$\text{Ca(HSO}_3)_2$]
Milky precipitate: Calcium chloride; Soluble clear compound: Calcium oxide
Milky precipitate: Calcium carbonate; Soluble clear compound: Calcium hydride
e: Explanation: Option 0 incorrectly identifies the milkiness as calcium sulphate. Option 1 is correct because when **Sulphur Dioxide ($\text{SO}_2$)** is bubbled through clear lime water [$\text{Ca(OH)}_2$], it forms an insoluble white precipitate of **Calcium Sulphite ($\text{CaSO}_3$)**, turning the liquid milky: $\text{Ca(OH)}_2 + \text{SO}_2 \rightarrow \text{CaSO}_3\downarrow + \text{H}_2\text{O}$. When **excess $\text{SO}_2$** is passed into the suspension, the insoluble sulphite reacts to form water-soluble **Calcium Bisulphite / Calcium Hydrogen Sulphite [$\text{Ca(HSO}_3)_2$]**, causing the white milkiness to completely disappear: $\text{CaSO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{SO}_2 \rightarrow \text{Ca(HSO}_3)_2$. This mirrors the $\text{CO}_2 / \text{Ca(HCO}_3)_2$ reaction pathway. Option 2 and Option 3 list non-sulphite calcium salts.

qe: Sulphur forms several non-crystalline allotropic modifications under distinct thermal and cooling conditions. What non-crystalline form of sulphur is produced when boiling liquid sulphur is poured suddenly into cold water?
qh: सल्फर अलग-अलग तापीय और शीतलन स्थितियों के तहत कई गैर-क्रिस्टलीय (अनाकार) अपररूपी परिवर्तनों का निर्माण करता है। जब उबलते हुए तरल सल्फर को अचानक ठंडे पानी में डाला जाता है तो सल्फर का कौन सा गैर-क्रिस्टलीय रूप बनता है?
o: Rhombic sulphur ($\alpha$-sulphur)
Plastic Sulphur (an amorphous, rubber-like supercooled liquid polymer)
Monoclinic sulphur ($\beta$-sulphur)
Flower of sulphur
e: Explanation: Option 0 lists rhombic sulfur, which is a crystalline octahedral form obtained by evaporating a $\text{CS}_2$ solution. Option 1 is correct because when liquid sulfur is boiled ($\\sim 444^\circ\text{C}$, breaking its $\text{S}_8$ rings into long polymeric chains) and then **quenched rapidly by pouring into cold water**, the sudden cooling prevents the sulfur atoms from reorganizing into a crystalline lattice. This yields **Plastic Sulphur**, a non-crystalline, soft, rubber-like **Amorphous Allotrope** consisting of entangled helical polymeric sulfur chains. Upon standing, plastic sulfur slowly recrystallizes back into stable rhombic $\alpha$-sulfur. Option 2 is crystalline monoclinic sulfur, and Option 3 is flower of sulfur (obtained by sublimation).

qe: Helox (a mixture of helium and oxygen) is used instead of compressed air by deep-sea divers during high-depth oceanic descents. What physiological and physical chemistry principle justifies replacing nitrogen with helium in breathing gas mixtures?
qh: गहरे समुद्र में गोताखोरों द्वारा उच्च गहराई वाले समुद्री अवरोहण के दौरान संपीड़ित हवा के बजाय हेलॉक्स (हीलियम और ऑक्सीजन का मिश्रण) का उपयोग किया जाता है। श्वसन गैस मिश्रण में नाइट्रोजन को हीलियम से बदलने को कौन सा शारीरिक और भौतिक रसायन सिद्धांत सही ठहराता है?
o: Helium oxidizes underwater nitrogen into solid salt crystals, preventing muscle cramps.
Helium exhibits extremely low solubility in blood even under high ambient pressures, preventing decompression sickness (the bends) and nitrogen narcosis.
Helium reacts with blood plasma to synthesize glucose, eliminating the need for diving rations.
Helium increases the weight of oxygen molecules, allowing divers to sink without lead weights.
e: Explanation: Option 0 incorrectly states helium oxidizes nitrogen gas into salt crystals. Option 1 is correct because according to **Henry's Law** [the mass of a gas dissolved in a given volume of liquid is directly proportional to the partial pressure of that gas in equilibrium with the liquid], nitrogen gas in ordinary compressed air dissolves into the blood and fatty tissues under high hydrostatic pressures experienced deep underwater. Rapid ascent causes dissolved nitrogen to bubble violently out of solution, causing severe joint pain and vascular blockages known as **Decompression Sickness (The Bends)**, while also inducing **Nitrogen Narcosis** [a reversible intoxicating effect on the central nervous system caused by high partial pressures of dissolved nitrogen]. **Helium ($\\text{He}$)** is utilized because it has an exceptionally **Low Blood Solubility** even under extreme hyperbaric pressures, minimizing tissue gas absorption and preventing nitrogen narcosis. Option 2 and Option 3 describe impossible glucose synthesis or heavy mass effects.

qe: Navigational safety lighting at aviation aerodromes relies on specialized noble gas lamps that remain visible to pilots even through dense atmospheric fog. Which noble gas powers these fog-penetrating airport lamps?
qh: उड्डयन एयरोड्रोम पर नेविगेशनल सुरक्षा लाइटिंग विशेष उत्कृष्ट गैस लैंपों पर निर्भर करती है जो घने वायुमंडलीय कोहरे के माध्यम से भी पायलटों को दिखाई देते हैं। कौन सी उत्कृष्ट गैस इन कोहरे को भेदने वाले हवाई अड्डे के लैंप को शक्ति प्रदान करती है?
o: Helium
Neon
Argon
Radon
e: Explanation: Option 0 refers to helium, which is used in weather balloons and cryogenics. Option 1 is correct because **Neon ($\\text{Ne}$)**, when subjected to high-voltage discharge in gas tubes, emits an intense reddish-orange spectrum with minimal light scattering by suspended atmospheric water droplets (Rayleigh scattering). These **Neon Lamps** produce high-intensity, long-wavelength illumination capable of penetrating thick fog, dust, and cloud cover, providing vital symbolic guidance to aircraft pilots along airport runways and approach beacons. Option 2 describes Argon (used for inert atmospheres in welding), and Option 3 describes Radon (a radioactive element used in cancer radiotherapy).

qe: Radioactive minerals like pitchblende, monazite, and cleveite contain trapped pockets of light noble gases. What nuclear physical process generates Helium ($\\text{He}$) inside these radioactive minerals over geological timescales?
qh: पिचब्लेंड, मोनाज़ाइट और क्लीवियाइट जैसे रेडियोधर्मी खनिजों में हल्की उत्कृष्ट गैसों के फंसे हुए जेब होते हैं। कौन सी परमाणु भौतिक प्रक्रिया भूवैज्ञानिक समय-सीमा में इन रेडियोधर्मी खनिजों के अंदर हीलियम ($\\text{He}$) उत्पन्न करती है?
o: Cosmic ray spallation of silica matrices.

Continuous accumulation of energetic Alpha Particles ($\\alpha$-particles, which are bare $^{4}_{2}\\text{He}^{2+}$ nuclei) emitted during the radioactive decay chains of heavy uranium and thorium isotopes.
Beta-decay of natural carbon-14 isotopes inside the crystal lattice.
Thermonuclear fusion of hydrogen gas inside earth's core.
e: Explanation: Option 0 confuses cosmic ray spallation (used to produce element Boron) with underground radioactive decay. Option 1 is correct because heavy radioactive elements present in pitchblende (uranium) and monazite (thorium) undergo spontaneous **Alpha Decay** [a radioactive disintegration process where an unstable parent nucleus ejects an alpha particle comprising two protons and two neutrons]. An **Alpha Particle** is physically identical to a bare **Helium Nucleus ($^{4}_{2}\\text{He}^{2+}$)**. As these alpha particles slow down within the dense mineral matrix, they capture two ambient electrons to become neutral **Helium Atoms ($\\text{He}$)**, remaining trapped inside the tight crystal lattice over millions of years. Option 2 and Option 3 describe beta decay or stellar core fusion.

qe: Boron Carbide ($\\text{B}_4\\text{C}$) is a non-metallic covalent network ceramic utilized in military armor and industrial nozzles. What is its commercial trade name, and what mechanical property justifies its use in bulletproof vests?
qh: बोरोन कार्बाइड ($\\text{B}_4\\text{C}$) एक गैर-धातु सहसंयोजक नेटवर्क सिरेमिक है जिसका उपयोग सैन्य कवच और औद्योगिक नोजल में किया जाता है। इसका व्यावसायिक व्यापार नाम क्या है, और कौन सा यांत्रिक गुण बुलेटप्रूफ जैकेट में इसके उपयोग को सही ठहराता है?
o: Carborundum; flexible liquid matrix that absorbs shock.
Norbide; extreme diamond-like crystal hardness combined with low density.
Borazole; soft self-lubricating sheet structure.
Graphene; transparent magnetic foil.
e: Explanation: Option 0 confuses Boron Carbide with Carborundum (Silicon Carbide, $\\text{SiC}$). Option 1 is correct because **Boron Carbide ($\\text{B}_4\\text{C}$)** is commercially known as **Norbide**. It is one of the hardest known artificial materials (ranking $\\sim 9.5+$ on the Mohs scale, just below diamond and cubic boron nitride). Its extreme **Crystal Hardness**, high compressive strength, and low density ($2.52\\text{ g/cm}^3$) allow it to shatter high-velocity armor-piercing projectiles upon impact, making it the premier ceramic material for lightweight military **Bulletproof Jackets** and body armor plates. Option 2 describes Borazole (inorganic benzene), and Option 3 describes graphene.

qe: Triborine Triammine ($\\text{B}_3\\text{N}_3\\text{H}_6$) displays structural, electronic, and physical similarities to the organic compound benzene ($\\text{C}_6\\text{H}_6$). What are its primary common chemical names?
qh: ट्राइबोरिन ट्राइअमाइन ($\\text{B}_3\\text{N}_3\\text{H}_6$) कार्बनिक यौगिक बेंजीन ($\\text{C}_6\\text{H}_6$) के साथ संरचनात्मक, इलेक्ट्रॉनिक और भौतिक समानताएं प्रदर्शित करता है। इसके प्राथमिक सामान्य रासायनिक नाम क्या हैं?
o: Carborundum or Norbide
Inorganic Benzene or Borazole (or Inorganic Graphite)
Boric Lotion or White Lead
Sorel Cement or Lithopone
e: Explanation: Option 0 lists silicon carbide or boron carbide trade names. Option 1 is correct because **Triborine Triammine ($\\text{B}_3\\text{N}_3\\text{H}_6$)** is commonly called **Inorganic Benzene** or **Borazole**. It features a cyclic six-membered ring structure consisting of alternating boron and nitrogen atoms with alternating single and double bonds, mimicking the planar $\\pi$-electron framework and physical constants of aromatic **Benzene ($\\text{C}_6\\text{H}_6$)** (it is isoelectronic and isosteric with benzene). Due to its structural arrangement, hexagonal boron nitride layers are also termed inorganic graphite. Option 2 lists eye washes or lead pigments, and Option 3 lists dental cements or paint pigments.

qe: Orthoboric Acid ($\\text{H}_3\\text{BO}_3$) is a weak, slippery inorganic acid of boron. What dual application does Orthoboric Acid serve in domestic recreational games and medical ophthalmology?
qh: ऑर्थोबोरिक अम्ल ($\\text{H}_3\\text{BO}_3$) बोरोन का एक कमजोर, फिसलन भरा अकार्बनिक अम्ल है। डोमेस्टिक मनोरंजक खेलों और मेडिकल नेत्र विज्ञान में ऑर्थोबोरिक अम्ल कौन सा दोहरा अनुप्रयोग प्रदान करता है?
o: Used as an explosive propellant in fireworks and as a dental tooth filling.
Used as a friction-reducing powder sprinkled on carrom boards and as a mild antiseptic eye wash under the name 'Boric Lotion'.
Used as a heavy metal solder flux and as a blood clotting agent.
Used as a high-temperature rocket fuel and as a skin dye.
e: Explanation: Option 0 misidentifies boric acid as an explosive or dental cement. Option 1 is correct because **Orthoboric Acid ($\\text{H}_3\\text{BO}_3$)** possesses a layered hydrogen-bonded sheet structure that easily shears under pressure, imparting a greasy, low-friction texture. Consequently, finely ground boric acid powder is sprinkled on **Carrom Boards** to reduce friction and allow smooth sliding of striker pieces. In pharmaceutical medicine, its weak antibacterial and antifungal properties make dilute aqueous solutions of orthoboric acid a standard mild **Antiseptic Eye Wash** commercially sold as **Boric Lotion**. Option 2 and Option 3 list unrelated metallurgical, explosive, or dye uses.

qe: Nuclear reactor safety depends on controlling the rate of sustained uranium neutron fission chain reactions. What physical property enables Boron ($\\text{B}$) rods to function as effective control rods in nuclear reactors?
qh: परमाणु रिएक्टर सुरक्षा निरंतर यूरेनियम न्यूट्रॉन विखंडन श्रृंखला प्रतिक्रियाओं की दर को नियंत्रित करने पर निर्भर करती है। कौन सा भौतिक गुण बोरोन ($\\text{B}$) छड़ों को परमाणु रिएक्टरों में प्रभावी नियंत्रण छड़ों (control rods) के रूप में कार्य करने में सक्षम बनाता है?
o: Boron acts as an explosive fuel that accelerates neutron speed.
Boron possesses an exceptionally high Neutron Capture Cross-Section, allowing it to absorb excess thermal neutrons without undergoing nuclear fission itself.
Boron reflects alpha radiation back into the containment shield.
Boron liquefies water to freeze the reactor core.
e: Explanation: Option 0 incorrectly states boron accelerates fission as a fuel. Option 1 is correct because the isotope Boron-10 ($^{10}\\text{B}$) has a remarkably high **Neutron Absorption Cross-Section** [a physical measure of the probability that an atomic nucleus will capture an incoming free neutron]. In a nuclear power plant, inserting **Boron Control Rods** (or boron steel/carbide alloys) into the reactor core allows operators to capture free thermal neutrons released by splitting $^{235}\\text{U}$ atoms: $^{10}_{5}\\text{B} + ^{1}_{0}\\text{n} \\rightarrow ^{7}_{3}\\text{Li} + ^{4}_{2}\\text{He}$. By absorbing surplus neutrons without decaying or fissioning itself, boron regulates or completely halts the nuclear chain reaction. Option 2 and Option 3 describe radiation reflection or core freezing.

qe: Modern microelectronics and high-speed semiconductor devices utilize Gallium Arsenide ($\\text{GaAs}$) computer chips. What performance advantage does Gallium Arsenide offer over traditional Silicon ($\\text{Si}$) in high-frequency electronic circuits?
qh: आधुनिक माइक्रोइलेक्ट्रॉनिक और उच्च गति वाले अर्धचालक उपकरण गैलियम आर्सेनाइड ($\\text{GaAs}$) कंप्यूटर चिप्स का उपयोग करते हैं। उच्च आवृत्ति वाले इलेक्ट्रॉनिक सर्किट में पारंपरिक सिलिकॉन ($\\text{Si}$) की तुलना में गैलियम आर्सेनाइड क्या प्रदर्शन लाभ प्रदान करता है?
o: GaAs is a liquid at room temperature that eliminates copper wiring.
GaAs possesses significantly higher Electron Mobility and a direct bandgap, enabling faster electron velocity, higher operating frequencies, and efficient optoelectronic emission.
GaAs dissolves in water to convert computer chips into biodegradable sugar.
GaAs acts as a superconductor at $500^\\circ\\text{C}$.
e: Explanation: Option 0 mischaracterizes GaAs as a room-temperature liquid. Option 1 is correct because **Gallium Arsenide ($\\text{GaAs}$)** is a compound semiconductor formed from Group-13 (Ga) and Group-15 (As) elements. Compared to elemental Silicon ($\\text{Si}$), GaAs possesses a much higher **Electron Mobility** [the measure of how quickly an electron can move through a semiconductor material when pulled by an electric field] and a **Direct Energy Bandgap**. This allows electrons to travel up to 5 times faster than in silicon, making GaAs computer chips superior for high-frequency radio frequency (RF) communications, optoelectronic photodiodes, solar cells, and high-speed satellite processors. Option 2 and Option 3 present water-dissolution or room-temperature superconductivity claims.

qe: Metalloids exhibit chemical and physical traits intermediate between metals and non-metals. Which choice lists the complete, recognized set of 7 metalloids in the Modern Periodic Table?
qh: उपधातु (Metalloids) धातुओं और गैर-धातुओं के बीच मध्यवर्ती रासायनिक और भौतिक लक्षणों को प्रदर्शित करते हैं। कौन सा विकल्प आधुनिक आवर्त सारणी में 7 उपधातुओं के पूर्ण, मान्यता प्राप्त समूह को सूचीबद्ध करता है?
o: Lithium, Sodium, Potassium, Rubidium, Cesium, Francium, Hydrogen
Boron ($\\text{B}$), Silicon ($\\text{Si}$), Germanium ($\\text{Ge}$), Arsenic ($\\text{As}$), Antimony ($\\text{Sb}$), Tellurium ($\\text{Te}$), and Polonium ($\\text{Po}$)
Helium, Neon, Argon, Krypton, Xenon, Radon, Oganesson
Iron, Cobalt, Nickel, Copper, Zinc, Silver, Gold
e: Explanation: Option 0 lists s-block alkali metals and hydrogen. Option 1 is correct because **Metalloids (Semimetals)** are elements positioned along the diagonal p-block boundary separating metallic elements from non-metallic elements. The standard set of 7 recognized metalloids includes **Boron ($\\text{B}$), Silicon ($\\text{Si}$), Germanium ($\\text{Ge}$), Arsenic ($\\text{As}$), Antimony ($\\text{Sb}$), Tellurium ($\\text{Te}$), and Polonium ($\\text{Po}$)**. They display intermediate electrical conductivity (semiconductors), amphoteric or weakly acidic oxides, and mixed covalent/metallic bonding properties. Option 2 lists Group-18 noble gases, and Option 3 lists transition metals.

qe: Superconducting magnets used in high-field Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectrometers and medical Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scanners require cryogenic operating conditions. Which liquid noble gas is deployed to maintain these superconducting coils below their critical temperatures?
